name_ja: しもつかれ／すみつかれ
name_en: Shimotsukare — daikon, soybean, and salted salmon head simmered in sake lees
summary_ja: 正月に残った塩鮭の頭と節分の炒り大豆、大根と人参を鬼おろしで粗くすりおろし、酒粕でじっくり煮込む冬の料理。初午の日にお稲荷様へ供え、余りを近所へ配る習わしが残る。栃木県など隣接地域にも同様の料理が伝わる。
summary_en: Leftover salted salmon head from New Year's and roasted soybeans from Setsubun are simmered with coarsely grated daikon and carrot in sake lees — a winter dish offered to the fox shrine on the first Horse Day of February, with leftovers shared among neighbors. Similar dishes are made in neighboring Tochigi.
source_title: しもつかれ／すみつかれ 茨城県

name_en: Niai — lotus root and burdock simmered and finished with vinegar
summary_ja: 水戸市東部の下市地方に伝わる、れんこんやごぼうを炒めてだしと醤油で煮て、仕上げに酢を回しかける料理。名は「煮て和える」からと伝わる。仏事では人参を抜き白く仕上げる作法もある。
summary_en: From the Shimoichi district east of Mito, lotus root and burdock are stir-fried, simmered in dashi and soy sauce, and finished with a splash of vinegar — the name is said to come from 'simmer and dress.' For Buddhist rites, carrot is left out to keep the dish white.

name_en: Hoshi Imo — sweet potato slices sun- and wind-dried into a chewy sweet
summary_ja: 蒸したさつまいもを薄切りにし、海風にさらして干し上げる保存食。静岡から伝わったとされ、ひたちなか市を中心に盛んに作られてきたとされる。素朴な甘さとねっとりした食感が持ち味。
summary_en: Steamed sweet potato is sliced thin and dried in the sea wind — a technique said to have come from Shizuoka, now centered on Hitachinaka, which leads the country in output. The result is naturally sweet with a chewy, dense bite.

name_ja: すだれ麩のごま酢和え
name_en: Sudare-bu no Goma Zu-ae — Yuki City's dried wheat-gluten cake dressed in sesame vinegar
summary_ja: 結城市だけでつくられる、小麦グルテンに再び小麦粉を練り込んで薄く延ばし、すだれで天日干しにした「すだれ麩」を、ごまと酢で和える一皿。城下町の精進料理から生まれたと伝わる。
summary_en: Made only in Yuki, wheat gluten is kneaded again with flour, rolled thin, and sun-dried on a bamboo screen — this 'sudare-fu' is then dressed with sesame and vinegar, a dish said to trace back to the old castle town's temple cooking.
source_title: すだれ麩のごま酢和え 茨城県

name_en: Komo Dofu — tofu pressed and boiled in a straw wrapper
summary_ja: 水切りした豆腐を藁苞に詰め、塩ゆでして固めた保存食。藁の跡が模様となり、ほのかな香りが移る。冠婚葬祭の料理として親しまれ、藁が手に入りにくくなり近年はつくる家庭が減っている。
summary_en: Drained tofu is packed into a straw wrapper and boiled in salted water until firm — the straw leaves a pattern and a faint aroma. Once common at weddings and funerals, it is made less often now that straw wrappers are harder to find.

name_en: Ogura Renkon — lotus root rings simmered sweet with red beans
summary_ja: 輪切りにしたれんこんの穴に小豆を詰めて甘く煮た正月料理。じっくり煮込むと筑波山が夕陽に赤く染まる様子から「紫峰色」と呼ばれる色に仕上がる。穴が見通せる縁起物として食べられる。
summary_en: Sliced lotus root has its holes packed with red beans and is simmered sweet for New Year's, taking on a purplish hue nicknamed 'Shiho color' after nearby Mt. Tsukuba at sunset — eaten as a good-luck charm for its 'clear view' holes.
source_title: 小倉れんこん 茨城県

name_en: Kabocha no Itokoni — pumpkin and red beans simmered for the winter solstice
summary_ja: かぼちゃと小豆を醤油と砂糖で煮た冬至の定番料理。保存がきくかぼちゃと邪気を払うとされる小豆の赤を合わせ、日照の短い時期を健やかに越すための料理として受け継がれてきた。
summary_en: Pumpkin and red beans are simmered in soy sauce and sugar for the winter solstice, pairing a keep-well squash with beans whose red is said to ward off misfortune — food meant to see people safely through the darkest days.
source_title: かぼちゃのいとこ煮 茨城県

name_en: Unagi no Hobiki-ni — eel simmered sweet and plated with a sail-boat motif
summary_ja: 酒と醤油、砂糖でふっくら煮たうなぎを、霞ヶ浦名物の帆引き船に見立てた笹の葉とともに供する料理。急な来客をもてなすため、冷凍していたうなぎを手早く仕上げる知恵から生まれたという。
summary_en: Eel is simmered soft in sake, soy sauce, and sugar, then plated with bamboo grass shaped to recall Lake Kasumigaura's sail-net fishing boats — a way, it is said, to turn frozen eel into a quick feast for unexpected guests.
source_title: うなぎの帆引き煮 茨城県

name_en: Kaiso Yose — seaweed jelly from the Kashima coast
summary_ja: 鹿島灘でとれる海藻・コトジツノマタを煮溶かし、型に流して冷やし固めた寒天状の料理。銚子の商人が正月前に売り歩いたことから、鹿行地域ではおせちの箸休めとして受け継がれている。
summary_en: Kotoji tsunomata seaweed from the Kashima coast is simmered until it thickens, then poured into a mold and chilled into a jelly-like dish — sold by Choshi merchants before New Year's, it lingers on Rokko-area tables as a palate cleanser.

name_ja: そぼろ納豆／しょぼろ納豆
name_en: Soboro Natto — Mito's small-grain natto mixed with dried daikon strips
summary_ja: 水戸で盛んな小粒納豆に、天日と寒風で干した割り干し大根を刻んで混ぜ、醤油やみりんで漬け込んだ保存食。糸引きの弱い納豆を活かす工夫から生まれたといい、方言で「しょぼろ納豆」とも呼ばれる。
summary_en: Mito's small-grain natto is mixed with sun- and wind-dried daikon strips and steeped in soy sauce and mirin — said to have started as a way to use natto that had not fermented quite right, and known locally as shoboro-natto.
source_title: そぼろ納豆／しょぼろ納豆 茨城県

name_ja: ピーナッツ味噌/落花生味噌
name_en: Pinattsu Miso — ground peanuts kneaded with miso and sugar
summary_ja: 国内有数の落花生産地・茨城県で、規格外の豆を無駄にしないよう考案された味噌和え。すり潰した落花生を味噌や砂糖と練り合わせ、ごはんのお供や酒の肴として常備菜にされる。
summary_en: In Ibaraki, one of Japan's top peanut-growing areas, this miso spread was devised to use peanuts too irregular for market — ground peanuts kneaded with miso and sugar, kept on hand as a rice topping or drinking snack.
source_title: ピーナッツ味噌/落花生味噌 茨城県

name_ja: いもがらの炒め煮/いもがらの五目煮
name_en: Imogara no Itameni — dried taro stems simmered with root vegetables
summary_ja: 里芋の茎を乾燥させた「いもがら」を水で戻し、れんこんや油揚げ、こんにゃくとともにじっくり煮た常備菜。豊富にとれる野菜を長く食べるための保存食の一つとして、正月にも食卓に並ぶ。
summary_en: Dried taro stems, imogara, are rehydrated and simmered slowly with lotus root, fried tofu, and konjac — one of several preserves born of a vegetable-rich region, and a dish that still appears at New Year's tables.
source_title: いもがらの炒め煮/いもがらの五目煮 茨城県

name_en: Renkon no Kinpira — lotus root, burdock, and carrot stir-fried sweet and salty
summary_ja: 国内生産量日本一を誇る霞ヶ浦周辺のれんこんを、ごぼうや人参とともに太めに切って甘辛く炒めたきんぴら。ふたをせずさっと仕上げることで、シャキシャキとした食感を残すのが特徴。
summary_en: Lotus root from around Lake Kasumigaura, the country's top producer, is cut thick with burdock and carrot and stir-fried sweet and salty — left uncovered on the heat to keep its crunch.
source_title: れんこんのきんぴら 茨城県

name_ja: 手作りさしみこんにゃく
name_en: Tezukuri Sashi Konnyaku — raw konjac sliced thin and eaten as sashimi
summary_ja: こんにゃく発祥の地とされる奥久慈地方で、精粉からつくるためアクが少なく、生のまま刺身で食べられるこんにゃく。わさびや柚子を添え、正月やもてなしの席で振る舞われてきた。
summary_en: In the Okukuji area, said to be where konjac processing began, refined-flour konjac has little bitterness and can be eaten raw as sashimi, garnished with wasabi or yuzu and served at New Year's and to guests.
source_title: 手作りさしみこんにゃく 茨城県

name_en: Shimi Konnyaku — konjac freeze-dried outdoors over winter
summary_ja: 厳冬期の畑にわらを敷き、こんにゃくを凍らせては昼の日差しで解かすことを20日ほど繰り返してつくる保存食。水分が抜けてスポンジ状になり、独特の食感で煮しめによく使われる。
summary_en: Konjac is laid on straw in midwinter fields and repeatedly frozen overnight and thawed by day for about 20 days, losing its moisture into a sponge-like texture prized in simmered dishes.
source_title: 凍みこんにゃく 茨城県

name_en: Ankou no Tomozu — boiled monkfish dipped in vinegared miso
summary_ja: ゆでたアンコウの身やヒレ、肝など複数の部位を、肝を練り込んだ酢味噌につけて食べる北部地域の冬の料理。西のフグ東のアンコウと並び称される茨城の冬の味覚として親しまれる。
summary_en: Boiled monkfish — flesh, fin, liver, and more — is dipped in a vinegared miso worked through with its own liver, a winter dish from the north coast often paired with fugu as one of Japan's twin winter delicacies.
source_title: あんこうの共酢 茨城県

name_en: Paita Yaki — minced sardine or saury pan-fried with miso and egg
summary_ja: 叩いたイワシやサンマにねぎ、しょうが、味噌、卵を混ぜて焼いた漁師料理。舟を漕ぐ櫂の平らな部分で魚を叩いたことから「パイタ」と呼ばれるようになったと伝わる、那珂湊の家庭の味。
summary_en: Minced sardine or saury is mixed with scallion, ginger, miso, and egg and pan-fried — a fisherman's dish said to be named for paita, the flat oar once used to pound the fish, now a Nakaminato home-cooking staple.
source_title: パイタ焼き 茨城県
